newsitem.title: FRANCE: French banks group unhappy over pension fund draft.
newsitem.headline: French banks group unhappy over pension fund draft.

text.p: The French banks association AFB questioned on Thursday the efficiency of proposed government legislation setting up private pension funds and predicted it would need amending after becoming law.

"We're not optimistic...because there are so many limits, ceilings put here and there at the initiative of ministers involved that we fear the savings funds will fall short of their goal," said AFB's managing director Patrice Cahart.
The measure would likely need revising after one or two years when it became apparent it "is not the solution to the problems facing us," he said.
He said a key problem was too low tax income deduction limits for contributions. Employee contributions can receive an income tax write-off of five percent of annual gross salary.

The measure would not allow those with only 10 to 15 years away to retirement enough time to amass a sufficient pension fund contribution, he said. "Five percent of gross income over 10 to 15 years is insufficient to accumulate a significant amount for a pension," he said.

"Over 30 years, the plan could have a significant impact on the amount (contributed)," he said. "The problem is that it is not those who are 30 years away from retirement who pose the problem, it's those who are 10 to 15 years away."
A Senate vote is due to be held on Friday on the bill which would allow the introduction of private pension funds in France, probably in 1998.
